title: Nitter and XCancel resume service after legal advice
why_read: Relevant update for developers relying on these Twitter/X front-end proxies, touching on legal and technical aspects of scraping and mirroring social media.
analysis: Nitter and XCancel are open-source alternative front-ends for Twitter/X that strip tracking and ads; their on-and-off legal status is a recurring story tied to platform API restrictions and takedown requests. This news is relevant to engineers who self-host or depend on these tools, and touches on broader issues of API gatekeeping and scraping legality. Not deeply technical itself, but of practical interest to a niche audience.
